extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and number theory familiar with Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory / IUTch series
extracted.subtask_description: Formulation and structural criteria for multiradiality of theta monoids (Kummer-compatible) within the IUT framework: definitions of radial/coric data, required splittings at bad primes, automorphism compatibilities, and the radial algorithm producing coric data from radial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer-compatible Multiradiality of Theta Monoids (Theorem 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed initial Θ-data and a Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater, the multiradial structure of theta monoids is Kummer-compatible: natural homomorphisms between automorphism groups of prime-strips exist (with certain second arrows surjective) and the Kummer isomorphisms of Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 1.5 are respected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated in Theorem 2.2, (i): the natural functors assigning to an F-prime-strip the associated F×μ-prime-strips determine natural homomorphisms (the second arrows in each line are surjections) that are compatible with the Kummer isomorphisms of Proposition 2.1, (ii), and Theorem 1.5, (iii). See final portions of Proposition 2.1, (iv)-(vi) for related compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphisms of Prime-strips must induce compatible surjective maps
rubrics_metrics.description: The automorphism groups of various F-prime-strips (and their associated ×μ-prime-strips) are linked by natural homomorphisms; in each relevant sequence the second arrow is a surjection and these maps are compatible with the Kummer isomorphisms used in the theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence of Theorem 2.2, (i). The natural functors F-prime-strip → F×μ-prime-strip composed with Proposition 2.1 isomorphisms yield the homomorphisms. Compatibility with Kummer isomorphisms and surjectivity of specific arrows are required for the multiradial constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer aspects of multiradiality at bad primes (submonoids and commutative diagram)
rubrics_metrics.description: At each v ∈ Vbad one must identify submonoids ∞Ψ⊥env(†D>)v ⊆ ∞Ψenv(†D>)v and ∞Ψ⊥Fenv(†HT Θ)v ⊆ ∞ΨFenv(†HT Θ)v corresponding to splittings; these fit into a commutative diagram (with natural inclusions, surjections, superscripts μ, ×, ×μ interpreted as torsion/units/quotients) compatible with various group actions, and certain composite maps (displayed) are equal to the zero map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the content of Theorem 2.2, (ii). The diagram involves poly-isomorphisms induced by inverse second Kummer isomorphisms, the final horizontal arrows determined by poly-automorphisms of prime-strips, and compatibility with group actions Gv(MΘ*). The final composite map ∞Ψenv(†D>)μ_v → Ψss_cns(†F)×μ_v is equal to the zero map (see '(bv)' and Proposition 2.1, (iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of auxiliary data at bad primes (av, bv, cv, dv)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ Vbad the multiradial construction requires the specific data (av) ∞Ψ⊥env(†D>)v ⊇ ∞Ψenv(†D>)μ_v; (bv) an identification Πμ(MΘ*) ⊗ Q/Z ∼→ ∞Ψenv(†D>)μ_v relative to natural isomorphisms; (cv) the projective system of mono-theta environments MΘ*; and (dv) splittings ∞Ψ⊥v obtained by restricting to zero-labeled evaluation points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four items are enumerated in Theorem 2.2, (ii) and are essential inputs to the commutative diagram and the Kummer-theoretic identifications at bad primes. See Proposition 2.1, Remark 1.5.2 and [IUTchII], Proposition 3.1, (i) for constructions and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Splittings determined by zero-labeled evaluation points
rubrics_metrics.description: The splittings ∞Ψ⊥ (used to avoid profinite (Z_hat)-translation indeterminacies) are achieved by restriction to zero-labeled evaluation points; these splittings permit restriction to Z-conjugates (discrete rigidity) rather than Z_hat-conjugates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed in Remark 2.1.2 (i) and used in Theorem 2.2, (ii). These 'complements on tempered coverings' (IUTchI §2) allow one to avoid (Z_hat)-translation indeterminacies and force coordinates of evaluation points to lie in Z rather than (Z_hat). This mechanism underlies 'evaluation discrete rigidity.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective amalgamation of Πv and Πμ via mono-theta environments
rubrics_metrics.description: The projective system of mono-theta environments constructed from Πv can be viewed as an 'amalgamation of Πv and Πμ' that allows reconstruction of the mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (not merely its (Z_hat)×-orbit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explained in Remark 2.2.1 (i): writing Πv, Πμ and (l·ΔΘ), the projective system built from Πv via the mono-theta environments permits reconstruction of the full cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism (cf. IUTchII Proposition 1.5, (iii)). This is essential to recover more than just the (Z_hat)×-orbit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kummer classes realized as twisted homomorphisms restricting to cyclotomic rigidity
rubrics_metrics.description: Kummer classes in ∞Ψ⊥env(†D>)v can be interpreted, after choosing a suitable characteristic open subgroup H ⊆ Πv, as twisted homomorphisms H → Πμ whose restriction to (l·ΔΘ) coincides with the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 2.2.1 (ii) spells out this viewpoint: the Kummer-theoretic link between étale-like data and Frobenius-like data at v is established via projective systems of mono-theta environments, and the Kummer classes behave like twisted homomorphisms compatible with the cyclotomic rigidity on (l·ΔΘ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insulation from (Z_hat)×-indeterminacies (mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mono-theta-theoretic cyclotomic rigidity isomorphism insulates the étale theta function from (Z_hat)×-indeterminacies that act on coric log-shell monoids '(−)×μ'; this decoupling lets one treat Πμ as 'purely radial' and the monoids '(−)×μ' as 'purely coric'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Remark 2.2.1 (ii)-(iv): because the Kummer-theoretic link is via projective mono-theta environments that do not involve '(−)×μ', the cyclotomic rigidity is immune to automorphisms of '(−)×μ'. Figures 2.1 and 2.2 illustrate induced vs. insulated (Z_hat)×-indeterminacies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of Kummer-compatible splittings via Galois evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiradial splittings must be Kummer-compatible and are realized by Galois evaluation at zero-labeled evaluation points; naive correspondences q ↦ q^λ (λ arbitrary positive integer) lack the multiradial machinery and fail to give Kummer-compatible splittings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed in Remark 2.2.2 (i),(iii) and Fig. 2.3: Galois evaluation and the F±-symmetry furnish the necessary splittings; attempts to replace the étale theta-function-based setup by q↦q^λ correspondences do not provide the apparatus to insulate Kummer classes from (Z_hat)×-indeterminacies and run into symmetry and Kummer-incompatibility problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radial data composition (definition: aR–eR)
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of radial data †R = (†HT D-Θ±ellNF, Fenv(†D>), †Rbad, F(cid:3)×μ(†D(cid:3)) , Fenv(†D> ) ∼→ F(cid:3)×μ(†D(cid:3))) must consist of: (aR) a D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theater; (bR) the associated F(cid:4)-prime-strip; (cR) the data (av),(bv),(cv),(dv) for v ∈ Vbad, denoted †Rbad; (dR) the associated F(cid:3)×μ-prime-strip; (eR) a full poly-isomorphism of the F(cid:3)×μ-prime-strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the precise specification in Corollary 2.3 (definition of radial environment). Each component (aR–eR) is required to construct the radial environment and to run the radial algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of radial data (aMorR–eMorR) must be compatible and induced
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism †R → ‡R of radial data consists of: (aMorR) an isomorphism of D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters; (bMorR) the induced isomorphism of F(cid:4)-prime-strips; (cMorR) the induced isomorphism between †Rbad and ‡Rbad; (dMorR) an isomorphism of F(cid:3)×μ-prime-strips induced by (aMorR); and (eMorR) the isomorphisms of (bMorR) and (dMorR) must be compatible with the poly-isomorphisms of (eR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.3 (definition of morphisms between radial data). Morphisms are tightly constrained to be induced by theater/prime-strip isomorphisms and to respect the poly-isomorphism structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coric data composition and morphisms (aC,bC; aMorC,bMorC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of coric data †C = (†D(cid:3), F(cid:3)×μ(†D(cid:3))) must consist of: (aC) a D(cid:3)-prime-strip †D(cid:3); (bC) the associated F(cid:3)×μ-prime-strip. A morphism between coric data consists of: (aMorC) an isomorphism of D(cid:3)-prime-strips; (bMorC) an isomorphism of F(cid:3)×μ-prime-strips that induces the isomorphism on associated D(cid:3)-prime-strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.3 (definitions). Coric data and their morphisms mirror the radial-data definitions but live on the coric/×μ side; inducedness and compatibility are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radial algorithm and functorial properties (full, essentially surjective, multiradial)
rubrics_metrics.description: The radial algorithm assigns radial data †R to coric data †C (†R ↦ †C) together with the induced assignment on morphisms; the associated functor is full and essentially surjective, and the radial environment is multiradial. Additionally: (ii) D-theaters indexed by n,m∈Z define associated radial data and poly-isomorphisms induce identifications; (iii) the poly-isomorphisms of F(cid:3)×μ-prime-strips are compatible with Kummer isomorphisms of Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 1.5; (iv) the algorithmic constructions (isomorphisms, Kummer isomorphisms, poly-isomorphisms) are stabilized/equivariant/functorial with respect to arbitrary automorphisms of domain and codomain horizontal arrows of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Corollary 2.3 (i)-(iv). The functorial and equivariance properties are essential: fullness/essential surjectivity guarantee the radial algorithm captures all coric structures up to isomorphism; compatibility with Kummer isomorphisms and equivariance under automorphisms ensures the constructions respect the broader Gaussian log-theta-lattice symmetries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of poly-isomorphisms with Gaussian log-theta-lattice arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: Poly-isomorphisms induced by vertical and horizontal arrows of the Gaussian log-theta-lattice must induce corresponding poly-isomorphisms of radial and coric data; identifications obtained by these poly-isomorphisms admit arbitrary permutation symmetries among the spokes (labels n∈Z) and are compatible with the étale-picture of D-Θ±ellNF-Hodge theaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary 2.3, (ii)-(iii): vertical arrows induce identifications n,mR ∼→ n,m+1R etc., producing n,◦R and n,◦C; horizontal arrows induce full poly-isomorphisms of D(cid:3)-prime-strips. Compatibility with IUTchII Corollary 4.11, (ii) is asserted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: Gaussian monoids require log-shell theory and have larger indeterminacies
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiradial techniques developed for theta monoids cannot be applied immediately to Gaussian monoids; the multiradiality of Gaussian monoids requires the log-shell theory developed in §1, and the resulting indeterminacies are more severe (though still manageable for the volume computations in IUTchIV) compared to the negligible root-of-unity indeterminacies in the theta-monoid case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 2.2.1 (iv) and Remark 2.2.2 (ii): Gaussian monoids depend crucially on log-shell constructions; the theta case's indeterminacies (multiplication by roots of unity) are mild because of the mono-theta Kummer theory, a property not directly available for Gaussian monoids.
